data.bottom_line: With so little information from this zone, it's hard to know how likely it is that a person could trigger an avalanche. What we know is that it has been 3 days since any new snow or significant wind that could create new snow problems. The most recent large storm was 4 days ago, which brought up to 2' of new snow above 2,000'. There was very little avalanche activity from this storm, based on what we could see from Seward. With limited information, an assessment mindset and a terrain progression are a good idea. If you get onto steep terrain, choose slopes with clean runouts in case you get surprised. __________________________________ SPECIAL ANNOUNCEMENTS: Forecast Operations: Daily danger ratings for Turnagain Pass begin Saturday, November 28. Weekly danger ratings for Chugach State Park and Summit Lake also begin on Saturday, November 28. On December 2nd and 3rd, the Northern Aspects Film Festival 2026 will be showing at Bear Tooth Theatrepub for its fifth year, celebrating the people, places, and stories that make skiing in Alaska unlike anywhere else. These showings will benefit the Hatcher Pass Avalanche Center and the Valdez Avalanche Center. Hope to see you there! Motorized Winter Access: Turnagain Pass opens to snowmachines on Wednesday, November 25, the day before Thanksgiving, per the CNF Forest plan and the new over-snow vehicle use map ( OSVU map ). The remaining motorized winter riding areas on the Chugach National Forest open December 1. Happy Thanksgiving from all of us at the Chugach National Forest Avalanche Center!
